newsitem.title: USA: NY conferees close to Power for Prosperity pact.
newsitem.headline: NY conferees close to Power for Prosperity pact.

text.p: The joint Senate/Assembly Conference Committee is close to agreement on a compromise between the "Power for Prosperity" bills that passed the two houses of the New York Legislature, Assembly Co-Chairman Paul Tonko told Reuters Thursday.
"We're moving close, I believe, to a compromise" after four meetings, including Thursday's split session, he said.
Senate Co-Chairman James Seward said there has been an agreement on a 400 megawatt program of low cost power for economic development and job preservation.
It also said the power would be purchased with competitive bids, a provision sought by the state's independent power producers -- commonly called IPPs.
Owners of New York IPPs include Besicorp Group Inc, CalEnergy Co Inc, Coastal Corp, ENSERCH Corp, GPU Inc, International Paper Co, LG&E Energy Corp, Marubeni Corp and PG&E Corp.
The Senate version called for a three year program providing 400 megawatts of power for large industrial cusomers.
Tonko said the committee has also "costed out" a 300 megawatt program.
He said the outstanding issues "come down to who's going to pay and how much its going to cost," adding he expects final language to be drafted Thursday and Friday.

The Assembly passed a bill calling for a 10 year program to supply 200 megawatts of job retention and creation power -- 125 to large industries and 75 to small business and not-for-profit users of less than 400 kilowatts.

Half of the power would come from the New York Power Authority's Fitzpatrick Nuclear Power Plant and half from the state's investor owned utilities -- Long Island Lighting Co, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Orange and Rockland Utilities Inc, Central Hudson Gas and Electric Corp, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, New York State Electric and Gas Corp and Rochester Gas and Electric Corp.
This version called for the utilities to be paid with credits against their gross receipt taxes, which the Senate had voted to end.
The conference is looking at a five year program with individual contracts limited to three years, Tonko spokesman Paul Larabee said.
Tonko said the compromise calls for bids to be sumitted on half the power being purchased and half to come from the Power Authority, which will conduct the bidding.
